heard_on_the_hill.headline: Mast releases China AI chip license data
heard_on_the_hill.body: House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast publicly released AI chip license information for China on November 19. CNBC reported he said Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies over the past six months, some to companies on the Pentagon's list of China military-linked companies. Mast also wrote to Commerce on Megaspeed, Energy and Commerce Chairman Guthrie requested briefings from Nvidia and Commerce, and a Senate committee plans joint testimony from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, per VOA Chinese.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Lawmakers object to Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia
heard_on_the_hill.body: Chairmen Mast, Moolenaar and Crawford released a statement on November 23 on Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang, and The Hill reported congressional Republicans are crying foul over President Trump's involvement while Democrats vow investigations and legislation. Rep. Michael McCaul pressed for an administration briefing on Huang's return; Huang and Nvidia had agreed on November 17 to appear before Congress.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: USCC sends 2026 annual report to Congress
heard_on_the_hill.body: The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission released its 2026 Annual Report to Congress on November 18. SCMP reported it urges Congress to declare China's detention of hundreds of Panama-flagged ships "economic coercion," and the Taipei Times reported it warns Beijing could resort to a blockade or quarantine of Taiwan if its political strategy appears to be failing.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: House report targets PRC open-weight AI models
heard_on_the_hill.body: Chairmen Garbarino and Moolenaar of the House Homeland Security Committee and the Select Committee on China released a joint investigative report on November 20 urging removal of PRC open-weight models from federal systems and high-risk critical infrastructure. The Select Committee said "China is Trying to Get U.S. Companies Addicted to Chinese AI Models," and CNBC reported SpaceX subsidiary Cursor told lawmakers it is considering dropping Chinese open-weight AI models.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Select Committee opens Mercedes-Benz China probe
heard_on_the_hill.body: Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar and Ranking Member Ro Khanna launched a bipartisan investigation on November 17 into Mercedes-Benz's ownership ties, technology partnerships and business relationships with entities in China, citing national security and supply chain concerns.
